title: An extension of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then $\mathcal F_2$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IE (schemes-lemma-extension-quasi-coherent), applied on an affine open cover (quasi-coherence is local); cf. perfect.tex Section 08CL: QCoh is a weak Serre subcategory

proof.text: Quasi-coherence is local on the scheme, so it suffices to work over an affine open U = Spec(A). Restriction of the given short exact sequence to U remains short exact: kernels are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and restriction to an open preserves cokernels because it preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (1); by its clause (2) F_1|_U and F_3|_U are quasi-coherent. The hypotheses identify the restricted end terms with associated modules M_1~ and M_3~, where M_i = F_i(U), by the affine quasi-coherent equivalence.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IE and Lemmas 01IA-01IB (affine-locality and the affine quasi-coherent equivalence)

proof.text: Write the restricted end terms as M_1~ and M_3~ and put M_2 = Γ(U, F_2). To prove 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0, injectivity and exactness in the middle follow from the sheaf axioms and the corresponding stalk exactness. For surjectivity, let m ∈ M_3 and let I = {a ∈ A | am lifts to M_2}. If p is a prime, choose a principal open D(f) containing p on which m lifts; then f ∉ p and f ∈ I after multiplying by a power, using the localization identifications on principal opens. For each point of V(f), choose a second principal open on which m lifts; the quasi-compactness of V(f) gives finitely many such opens and one common exponent. The resulting local lifts differ by sections of M_1 on overlaps; localization again kills these differences after a further common power, so the lifts glue to a global lift of f^N m. Thus I is contained in no prime, hence I = A and 1 ∈ I. Since F_2|_U is not yet known to be quasi-coherent, clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] cannot be applied to it; instead let ε: M_2~ → F_2|_U be the map corresponding to id_{M_2} under the adjunction of clause (1). For r ∈ A, the principal open D(r) ≅ Spec(A_r) is affine, the sequence restricted to D(r) is still short exact, and its end terms are (M_1)_r~ and (M_3)_r~ by the localization identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; so the argument above, run on D(r), gives an exact sequence 0 → (M_1)_r → F_2(D(r)) → (M_3)_r → 0. Localizing 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 at r is also exact (localization is exact), and under M_2~(D(r)) = (M_2)_r the component ε_{D(r)} is the map (M_2)_r → F_2(D(r)) induced by restriction; it is compatible with the isomorphisms (M_i)_r ≅ F_i(D(r)) for i = 1, 3. By the five lemma ε_{D(r)} is bijective. The principal opens form a basis of U, and a morphism of sheaves bijective on a basis of opens is an isomorphism, so ε is an isomorphism and F_2|_U ≅ M_2~ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. This is the principal-open argument of Schemes Lemma 01IE, written out rather than assumed.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IE (schemes-lemma-extension-quasi-coherent), affine proof on principal opens

proof.text: Every point of X lies in an affine open of the preceding kind, and quasi-coherence is defined by the existence of such affine presentations. Therefore the local quasi-coherence of F_2|_U for the affine cover implies that F_2 is quasi-coherent on X.
